data.gender_notes: Ujjaini is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is victorious over all difficulties. The name Ujjaini carries the meaning “Victorious One” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Ujjaini usually hope their child will grow to embody victorious one and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for a child who is destined to overcome all obstacles in life and reach spiritual enlightenment
data.etymology: Ujjaini belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Victorious One.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ujjaini total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ujjaini holds great historical and cultural significance in India, particularly in the region of Madhya Pradesh where the ancient city of Ujjain is located. Ujjain has been a center of Hindu learning, culture, and pilgrimage for many centuries. The city is famous for numerous temples, including the Mahakaleshwar Temple which is considered one of the twelve Jyotirlingas - the sacred abodes of the Hindu god Shiva. The name Ujjaini is reminiscent of the spiritual and historical importance of this city and its rich Hindu heritage.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ujjaini carries a deep spiritual significance as it translates to one who overcomes all obstacles and difficulties. In Hindu philosophy, life is seen as a journey filled with challenges and obstacles. The name Ujjaini encapsulates the spirit of resilience, courage, and determination that is required to navigate through life's tribulations. It is a reminder that no matter how difficult the path may be, one can emerge victorious and overcome all obstacles with the right mindset and effort.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ujjaini, derived from the ancient city Ujjain in Madhya Pradesh, symbolizes the inner radiance and enlightenment, much like the city being the spiritual center of ancient times. The name signifies the pursuit of self-improvement and inner joy, aligning oneself with the divine.

historical_references.reference: Ujjaini was an ancient Indian city, capital of the Avanti Mahajanapada, which existed from the 6th to the 4th century BC. It is located in present-day Madhya Pradesh, India. The city was an important center of learning and culture, with many temples and universities. It is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures and is an important pilgrimage site for Hindus today.
historical_references.context: Ancient Indian city, capital of Avanti Mahajanapada, important center of learning and culture

historical_references.reference: Ujjaini was also the capital of the Malava kingdom during the medieval period, from the 6th to the 13th centuries AD. It was an important center of Hinduism and Jainism, and was renowned for its temples and learning institutions. It was a major trading center, which attracted merchants from throughout India and beyond.
historical_references.context: Medieval capital of Malava kingdom, important center of Hinduism and Jainism, major trading center

modern_usage.modern_context: The ancient Hindu name 'Ujjaini' is gaining popularity in modern contexts due to its association with holistic living, spiritual tourism, and wellness. On Instagram, Ujjaini is seen as a hashtag for posts related to spirituality, yoga, and travel to the Ujjaini temple in India. On Pinterest, there are boards dedicated to Ujjaini as a spiritual and cultural destination, with pins featuring yoga poses, temple architecture, and traditional Indian clothing. On Blogger, there are several travel blogs that detail the history and significance of Ujjaini as a spiritual center and provide tips for planning a visit. Overall, the name 'Ujjaini' represents a connection to traditional Indian spiritual practices and is being embraced by modern audiences seeking authentic spiritual experiences and holistic living.
